focus: Pre-v4 corpus evidence, what the eras actually look like
noveltyJustification: Five findings are fully new (header version spread, naming drift, missing generated metadata counts, the containment double-count pitfall, the era bundle); one consolidates the stage map and counts as half new.
ruledOut: Trusting raw find counts for scope

label: Old template header versions exist and are measurable: resource-map v1.1 appears 224 times against v2.2 98 times, plus handover v1.0 (66) and research v1.0 (48); v2.2 dominates the core docs.

Header naming drift breaks naive version detection: implementation-summary appears as impl-summary-core (3,618), implementation-summary-core (176) and implementation-summary (95); decision-record appears as decision-record (711) and decision-record-core (30); a classifier needs the level manifest plus a pinned alias table and an unknown-header class.

Pre-generated-metadata packets exist in the archive: of 2,281 archived numbered dirs (excluding containment and research copies), 74 lack description.json and 77 lack graph-metadata.json, while live top-level packets have zero; create.sh always generates both, so these predate the metadata era.

Corpus-wide tooling must exclude non-packet copies: including this lineage's containment baseline (a full specs copy) inflated the archived count from 2,281 to 8,198; heal-spec-docs.cjs keeps a skip list and its own comment records its packet-name regex is the fourth copy of the same pattern.

Old-format classes map to existing stages: no frontmatter to fill-frontmatter; missing/non-matching headers to heal-spec-docs; missing generated metadata and stale paths to migrate-generated-json and repair-derived; anchors have no stage; missing docs stay lane work with dated notes.

Pre-v4 is not one era but a bundle of independent ones (pre-frontmatter docs, old header versions, pre-metadata packets, naming variants), so detection must report per-class counts and route each class to its own stage rather than emit one version verdict. (INFERRED from the measured class spread; confirmable by running the census once built.)
